title: The normalized affine-space exceptional coefficient mate on the ordinary etale site
statement: Let $k$ have characteristic $p>0$, $\ell\ne p$ prime, $V$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $\pi:\mathbf A^r_V\to V$ projection for $r\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-affine-space]. Let $A=\mathcal O_E/t^m$, $B=\mathcal O_F/v^n$, $m,n\geq1$, be coefficient stages of finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $A\to B$ a unital map [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use ordinary etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], $F_R=R\pi_{!,R}$ for the standard compactification [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and its ambient right adjoint $\pi_R^\times$ normalized by vector-bundle integration [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity]. Put $T=-\otimes_A^LB$ [def-kun-derived-tensor] and let $q:T_VF_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_{\mathbf A^r_V}$ be the canonical coefficient projection. For $L$ bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude], the $F_B\dashv\pi_B^\times$ transpose $b_\pi:T\pi_A^\times L\to\pi_B^\times TL$ of $T\epsilon_{A,L}\circ q_{\pi_A^\times L}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Under the counit-preserving identifications $\pi_R^\times L\cong\pi^*L(r)[2r]$ it is the canonical coefficient/twist reassociation. Its transport under etale/pro-etale site equivalence is the specified smooth coefficient mate of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional].

source.place: Charts and uniqueness of transposes; the site/coefficient square is the separately cited lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility, and the transported counit is det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer.

proof.text: Write $X=\mathbf A^r_V$, $T_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ and $H_RK=\pi^*K(r)[2r]$. The coefficient definition gives finiteness of $A,B$. In each valuation ring $|\ell|=\ell^{-1}<1$, so $\ell$ belongs to its maximal ideal, generated by its uniformizer; therefore $\ell^mA=0$ and $\ell^nB=0$. Take a common annihilator $N=\ell^{\max(m,n)}$, invertible over $k$. The field $k$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal; the finite-type theorem makes $V$ Noetherian. The coordinate-tower statement makes $X$ Noetherian and $\pi$ separated of finite type. The standard compactification stages are proper over standing bases, hence finite type; the same finite-type theorem makes them Noetherian. The chart-domain theorem applies to $A\to B$, with no flatness requirement: $T$, $H_R$ and the chosen compact-support functors preserve $D^b_{ctf}$, and site comparison is an equivalence there. These are the domains on which all following coefficient and site maps are evaluated.

source.place: Hypotheses for Charts, and the finite-stage domains of its coefficient and site comparisons.

proof.text:
Put $W_R=R_X(r)[2r]$ and let $t_R:F_RW_R\to R_V$ be vector-bundle integration. For the globally trivial bundle, use the single trivialization over $V$ in its defining construction: $t_R$ is exactly the ordered affine-space counit at $R_V$. Let $w:T_XW_A\xrightarrow{\sim}W_B$ be the canonical coefficient/Tate/shift identification. Specialize the affine coefficient-counit equation to $K=A_V$; the canonical unit identification $T_VA_V=B_V$ identifies $a_{r,A_V}$ with $w$. It gives the actual equality
$$t_B\circ F_B(w)\circ q_{W_A}=T_V(t_A).$$
The affine counit lemma specifies the coefficient map for every fixed compactification, so this is the $q$ of the item, including the standard compactification. This step only uses the affine counit at the unit; it does not identify an arbitrary counit from its value at the unit.

source.place: Charts: coefficient compatibility of the iterated projective-line integration, evaluated at the coefficient unit.

proof.text:
For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(V,A)$ let $a_K:T_XH_AK\xrightarrow{\sim}H_BT_VK$ be the canonical scalar/pullback, twist and shift comparison from the affine counit lemma. Write $P_{R;K,M}:K\otimes_R^LF_RM\to F_R(\pi^*K\otimes_R^LM)$ for the coefficient-first projection map and
$$z_{R,K}=(1_K\otimes t_R)\circ P_{R;K,W_R}^{-1}:F_RH_RK\to K,$$
with tensor unitors understood. These are precisely the integration maps whose ambient transposes are the purity isomorphisms. The compact-support scalar/projection coherence equation, followed by naturality of $P_B$ in $w$, reads
$$F_B(a_K)\circ q_{H_AK}\circ T_V(P_{A;K,W_A})=P_{B;T_VK,W_B}\circ(1\otimes(F_B(w)\circ q_{W_A})).$$
Multiply by the inverse projection maps and then $1\otimes t_B$. The trace equality in Step 2 changes the right-hand side to $1\otimes T_V(t_A)$, so
$$z_{B,T_VK}\circ F_B(a_K)\circ q_{H_AK}=T_V(z_{A,K}).$$
The scalar/projection lemma concerns the same proper-counit/open-tensor coefficient map as $q$; its hypotheses allow arbitrary $B$ over $A$. All inverse projection maps here are the ones in the vector-bundle purity formula.

source.place: Charts: expand the tensor-normalized counit at a complex using coefficient compatibility of projection and of the trace. Projection coherence uses Stacks Tag 0GL6, remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings, through the cited coherence node.

proof.text:
Let $\gamma_{R,K}:H_RK\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_R^\times K$ be exactly the integration-transposed map of vector-bundle purity. By its definition as an adjunction transpose,
$\epsilon_{R,K}\circ F_R(\gamma_{R,K})=z_{R,K}$.
Set $d_K=\gamma_{B,T_VK}\circ a_K\circ T_X(\gamma_{A,K}^{-1})$. Naturality of $q$ at $\gamma_{A,K}^{-1}$ gives
$$q_{H_AK}^{-1}\circ F_B(T_X\gamma_{A,K}^{-1})=T_V(F_A\gamma_{A,K}^{-1})\circ q_{\pi_A^\times K}^{-1}.$$
Using Step 3, compute
$$\epsilon_{B,T_VK}\circ F_B(d_K)=T_V(z_{A,K})\circ q_{H_AK}^{-1}\circ F_B(T_X\gamma_{A,K}^{-1})=T_V(\epsilon_{A,K})\circ q_{\pi_A^\times K}^{-1}.$$
The Hom bijection defining an adjunction transpose is injective, hence $d_K=b_{\pi,K}$. Each factor defining $d_K$ is invertible, so $b_{\pi,K}$ is invertible. Equivalently,
$$\gamma_{B,T_VK}^{-1}\circ b_{\pi,K}\circ T_X(\gamma_{A,K})=a_K.$$
This proves the requested reassociation under the specified integration-normalized identifications. The displayed formulas are natural in $K$ since their constituents are; $\pi_A^\times K$ lies in the comparison domain by its isomorphism with $H_AK$ from Step 1.

source.place: Charts and uniqueness of transposes: compute the actual ambient transpose, rather than infer invertibility from invertibility of the left coefficient map.

proof.text:
The affine-space smoothness statement gives smoothness of pure relative dimension $r$, as required for the named smooth mate. For $R=A,B$, write $C_{T,R}=\nu_T^*$, $c_R:C_{V,R}F_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_R^{pro}C_{X,R}$ and $\delta_T:T_TC_{T,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{T,B}T_T$ for the specified site and scalar comparisons. The chart-domain theorem supplies the finite-Tor equivalences. Transfer the restricted ambient adjunction using the counit formula
$$\widetilde\epsilon_{R,C_{V,R}K}=C_{V,R}(\epsilon_{R,K})\circ c_R(\pi_R^\times K)^{-1}.$$
This restriction is an adjunction since both ambient functors preserve the full subcategories, as shown above. Transfer also $b_\pi$, using $\delta$ to identify its endpoints. Substitute the displayed counit formula into its transpose equation in Step 4. The site/coefficient square of the coefficient-compatibility lemma moves $c_A,c_B$ across $q$ and identifies the transferred left coefficient map with the specified pro-etale one $q^{pro}$, giving
$$\widetilde\epsilon_B\circ F_B^{pro}(\overline b_\pi)=T_V(\widetilde\epsilon_A)\circ(q^{pro})^{-1}.$$
The transfer lemma identifies the transferred right adjoints with the constructible exceptional adjoints by a counit-preserving isomorphism. Thus this is exactly the defining equation for $c_{A,B}(C_{V,A}K)$ in the smooth coefficient-mate statement, with $f=\pi$. Uniqueness of its transpose identifies it with $\overline b_\pi$. The Tate, pullback and shift factors in this transport use the canonical comparisons specified by the chart-domain theorem. At $r=0$ the affine adjunction and trace are identities, and all the equations reduce to the coefficient-unit identities; the empty base and $K=0$ are included without change.

source.place: Charts: transport the specified coefficient-counit identity through the site/coefficient square and the counit-preserving adjunction transfer.
